title: Over Every Door
author: a grandmother
pages:
Garlic over every door, and the back door too, which your father forgets.

No washing left out after dusk. It likes a cloak.
If the fog comes in pale and low, bring the goats in and stop the chimney.
If one of you is bitten, send to the fen for leeches the same night. They take the bad blood and are none the worse.
If you bring the cloaked one down, do not stand over it. It gets up again smaller, and it flies.
